command:
set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp

echo "== verify staged inputs against their pinned sha256 =="
{ printf '%s  %s\n' c686564b490098a9de36c6738206496b746f69739fb11855cfb9cdad958e0d4b pfam38.2_first200.hmm
  printf '%s  %s\n' 9b43da92651b35814597af6a8b18f500b768679a49fa4678224f384917ce7668 ensembl116_pep.fa.gz
} > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256

# hmmsearch cannot read a gzipped sequence database, so decompress first. gzip is
# a base-image utility, not a second scientific tool: this is still one tool, one task.
gzip -dc ensembl116_pep.fa.gz > pep.fa

echo "== hmmsearch: 200 Pfam 38.2 models vs the Ensembl 116 human proteome =="
hmmsearch --cpu 8 --tblout hits.tbl -o hmmer.out pfam38.2_first200.hmm pep.fa

# ---- smoke check ----
# hmmsearch is deterministic: the same version over the same two inputs gives the
# same numbers every time. The bands below are still bands, because a future HMMER
# version may legitimately shift hit counts; they are wide enough for that and
# tight enough that an empty, truncated or wrong-database search fails. Measured
# values are in the README's Observed column.
QUERIES=$(grep -c '^Query:' hmmer.out || true)
TARGETS=$(awk '/Target sequences:/ {print $3; exit}' hmmer.out)
HITS=$(grep -vc '^#' hits.tbl || true)
MODELS_WITH_HITS=$(grep -v '^#' hits.tbl | awk '{print $3}' | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
STRONG=$(grep -v '^#' hits.tbl | awk '$5 < 1e-10' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
# hmmsearch writes a literal "[ok]" as its last line only on clean completion.
# This is the check that catches a search killed part-way with a partial tblout.
TRAILER=$(tail -n 1 hmmer.out)

{
  echo "models_searched     $QUERIES              want exactly 200"
  echo "target_sequences    $TARGETS              want exactly 382428"
  echo "tblout_hits         $HITS                 want  40000..80000   (observed 59840)"
  echo "models_with_a_hit   $MODELS_WITH_HITS     want    140..200     (observed   168)"
  echo "hits_at_E_lt_1e-10  $STRONG               want   5000..20000   (observed 10050)"
  echo "hmmsearch_trailer   $TRAILER              want exactly [ok]"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt

test "$QUERIES"           -eq 200
test "$TARGETS"           -eq 382428
test "$HITS"              -ge 40000
test "$HITS"              -le 80000
test "$MODELS_WITH_HITS"  -ge 140
test "$MODELS_WITH_HITS"  -le 200
test "$STRONG"            -ge 5000
test "$STRONG"            -le 20000
test "$TRAILER"            = "[ok]"
test -s hits.tbl

gzip -n -6 hmmer.out          # 75 MB of per-domain detail compresses to a few MB
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
